thesis: Emotions are situated processes linking organisms, histories, interpretations and relationships.
role: Connects biological regulation to felt significance and social feeling rules.

ideas.statement: Emotion can prioritize action without infallibly judging a situation; function is distinct from experience.
Statistical categories and bodily expressions do not by themselves identify emotional ontology.
Labels and feeling rules can reveal suffering or redistribute emotional obligations and conceal exploitation.

evidenceAndExamples.statement: A photograph’s significance depends on memory and relationship rather than pigment alone.
Art can organize authentic emotion under represented rather than immediate danger.

objectionsAndQualifications.statement: Emotion theories remain disputed and video-derived categories are not a final taxonomy.

audit.notes: Every unit read; metaphysical commitments separated from empirical findings.
